rationale: C15 is the child’s expressly identified immediately preceding report and supplies a concrete, material template for it. The child repeats C15’s opening statutory-reporting formula, reporting-period linkage, numbered organization, treatment of the Iranian Transactions and Assets Control Regulations, licensing and enforcement activity, Claims Tribunal statistics, Security Account replenishment, large and small claims, government-to-government claims, bank-syndicate settlements, and a nearly verbatim concluding rationale. C19 and C17 are earlier reports in the same Iran reporting series and share substantial machinery, but C15 is the direct and strongest drafting source.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I hereby report to the Congress on developments since my last report of November 29, 1990, concerning the national emergency with respect to Iran... This report covers events through March 31, 1991
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I hereby report to the Congress on developments since the last report of May 14, 1990, concerning the national emergency with respect to Iran... This report covers events through September 30, 1990
shared_material.explanation: The child reuses the parent’s opening reporting formula and updates only the prior-report and coverage dates.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The great majority of import licensing activity under the ITRs involved the importation of nonfungible Iranian-origin goods, principally carpets, that were located outside Iran prior to the imposition of the embargo and that did not result in any payment or benefit accruing to Iran
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The major focus of licensing activity under the ITRs remains the importation of certain non-fungible Iranian-origin goods, principally carpets, which were located outside Iran before the embargo was imposed, and where no payment or benefit accrued to Iran
shared_material.explanation: This is distinctive shared language describing the same licensing category, with only light redrafting.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Tribunal continues to make progress in arbitrating the various claims before it... The Tribunal continues to make progress in the arbitration of claims of U.S. nationals for $250,000 or more.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Iran-United States Claims Tribunal... continues to make progress in arbitrating the claims before it... The Tribunal continues to make progress in the arbitration of claims of U.S. nationals for $250,000.00 or more.
shared_material.explanation: The child preserves the parent’s sequence and phrasing for Tribunal-wide statistics followed by the large-claims docket.

shared_material.parent_excerpt: The situation reviewed above continues to implicate important diplomatic, financial, and legal interests of the United States and its nationals and presents an unusual challenge to the national security and foreign policy of the United States.
